title: Give every payment row its own transaction

blocks.text: The treasury team imports the bank's payment file every night, one CSV row per payment. A row without an amount must be rejected and leave nothing behind, while the rows before and after it are imported. Last week a bad row left a "payment from" entry with no amount in the ledger, and reconciliation took a day.

`importRow` is already marked `@Transactional`, and `PaymentImport.transactional(...)` is the proxy that runs such methods in a transaction. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/PaymentImport.java`:

items: `CsvRows.importAll(...)`: import the rows, rejecting the bad ones;
`create(...)`: build the importer the application calls.

blocks.text: When you're done, each good row commits on its own, a bad row rolls back only itself and shows up in `rejected()`, and the ledger holds only complete payments. You may add a field. About six lines in total.

cases.says: a file of good rows ends up in the ledger in order, with nothing rejected
a row without an amount is rejected and the rows around it are imported
every good row commits a transaction of its own, and a bad row rolls back only its own
a rejected row leaves no partial entry in the ledger

origin.section: A Call the Target Makes on this Never Reaches the Proxy

concepts: A call the target makes on this goes straight to the target and never reaches the proxy, so behaviour attached to the called method is skipped; the call must go through the proxy reference.
